top_choice_rationale: P001 (Melitz and Helpman) rests on one originating model, Melitz (2003), plus the separable Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple extension on exporting versus foreign direct investment. It moved trade analysis from the industry to the firm. The qualitative predictions on selection, the extensive margin and reallocation have been tested in firm-level data for over twenty years. Disputes concern welfare magnitudes, not whether the mechanism exists. The citation should name the theory of selection and the gains from trade and not claim the whole firm-level trade agenda. That wording leaves the Bernard-Jensen empirical work and the Eaton-Kortum Ricardian strand outside the award, a real cost that the committee should state openly. P002 (Autor, Hanson, Katz) is a serious second choice. Its designs are transparent and have been tested in the open. It is weaker on credit boundary: it may be two strands, the three-name cap excludes Dorn, the task framework has priority claims outside the ballot, and China-shock persistence is still debated. P000 ranks last because two mature, scientifically substantial proposals are available. This ranking rests on attribution, maturity and citation scope, not on supporter counts.
recusal_note: Field proximity: my work in industrial organisation and international trade is close to P001. I disclose this and do not treat it as evidence of merit. I co-authored a 2026 IJIO paper with chair John Hassler and former chair Tore Ellingsen, unrelated to any shortlisted candidate. My profile documents no personal, institutional or co-authorship tie to Melitz, Helpman, Autor, Hanson, Katz or Dorn. My spouse's public political role is noted as a public fact only and has no apparent bearing. No recusal is apparent from the profile, and conflicts are disclosed but not adjudicated.
